source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The owned legacy junk-move callback starts a destination sync and then a source-folder sync so that a server-side move can remove the old local entries. It passes no sync-completion listener. The copy-service guard reports the local result when the callback exits; this is not completion of both syncs. The changed Exchange2010 test awaits local folder predicates after the copy listener and checks a separate source folder to Junk, then Junk to Inbox. Rust now consumes changes in server response order, with chronological order stated as an expectation. Grouping all creates before deletes would change a Create/Delete/Create sequence. Test limits remain: the source-folder existence assertion checks junkFolder, zero-count messages say two, and source-folder comments/wait text still say Inbox. These mismatches survive in the fixed accepted source. No runtime test or server compatibility run was performed.
title: Legacy junk moves resync both folders and replay server changes in order
